premise: Autumn leaves come twirling down and Hedgehog piles them up for his winter bed, but the wind huffs and puffs and blows his pile away twice; his scattered leaves bring Squirrel and Badger, they build the bed together down in a hollow, and this time the wind can't blow it away.
inspiration: The Three Little Pigs (English folk), turned gentle: the wolf is only the autumn wind, nobody is in danger, and the bed that stands is the one built low, by three friends together — the Little Red Hen's lonely work turned round too.
lesson: Hard jobs go better with friends.
learning: Hedgehogs gather dry leaves to make a cosy nest for their winter sleep.

en-US.title: Hedgehog Makes a Leaf Bed
en-US.text: {canvas:leaves 0.6} [softly] Autumn had come, and red and gold leaves came twirling down. {hedgehog:enter} Hedgehog needed a bed of dry leaves, to sleep in all winter long. {hedgehog:face happy} One leaf, two leaves, three… a lovely pile. {canvas:wind 0.8} {sfx:gust} But the wind huffed and puffed and WHOOSH! {hedgehog:face surprised} {hedgehog:spin} Off flew his bed. [gasps] Hedgehog started again. One leaf, two leaves… WHOOSH! {hedgehog:face sad} [sad] Gone again. His leaves landed on {squirrel:enter} Squirrel and {badger:enter} Badger, so {squirrel:go to hedgehog} {badger:go to hedgehog} over they came. {hedgehog:live talk} "The wind keeps taking my bed," sighed Hedgehog. {badger:live scratch-head} Badger thought. "Then make it where the wind can't reach." He {badger:live dig} dug a snug hollow, down low. Together they filled it with crackly leaves, and Squirrel {squirrel:live bury} patted them down. {sfx:crunch} Crunch, crunch. {hedgehog:face happy} In snuggled Hedgehog. The wind huffed. The wind puffed. But it couldn't blow this bed away, {canvas:wind stop} so off it went to blow somewhere else. {hedgehog:live curl hold} Hedgehog curled up, warm and prickly. [whispers] "Goodnight, Hedgehog," whispered his friends. {squirrel:face happy} {badger:face happy} {badger:hearts} {squirrel:hearts} "See you in the spring." {canvas:leaves stop}

es-ES.title: La cama de hojas de Erizo
es-ES.text: {canvas:leaves 0.6} [softly] Llegó el otoño, y las hojas caían dando vueltas, rojas y doradas. {hedgehog:enter} Erizo necesitaba una cama de hojas secas para dormir todo el invierno. {hedgehog:face happy} Una hoja, dos hojas, tres… ¡un buen montón! {canvas:wind 0.8} {sfx:gust} Pero el viento sopló y sopló y… ¡FIUUU! {hedgehog:face surprised} {hedgehog:spin} Adiós, cama. [gasps] Erizo volvió a empezar. Una hoja, dos hojas… ¡FIUUU! {hedgehog:face sad} [sad] Otra vez nada. Las hojas cayeron sobre {squirrel:enter} Ardilla y {badger:enter} Tejón, que {squirrel:go to hedgehog} {badger:go to hedgehog} vinieron a ver. {hedgehog:live talk} —El viento se me lleva la cama —suspiró Erizo. {badger:live scratch-head} Tejón se rascó la cabeza. —Pues hazla donde no llegue. Y {badger:live dig} cavó un hoyito, bien abajo. Entre los tres lo llenaron de hojas crujientes, y Ardilla {squirrel:live bury} las apretó con las patitas. {sfx:crunch} Cruj, cruj. {hedgehog:face happy} Erizo se metió dentro. Y el viento sopló y sopló, pero esta cama no se la llevó. {canvas:wind stop} Así que se fue a soplar a otra parte. {hedgehog:live curl hold} Erizo se hizo una bola calentita. [whispers] —Buenas noches, Erizo —susurraron sus amigos. {squirrel:face happy} {badger:face happy} {badger:hearts} {squirrel:hearts} —Hasta la primavera. {canvas:leaves stop}
